headline: The dollar blinked and duration rallied a third day, but crude took the week anyway — the tightening has moved from the curve to the barrel and the peso.
summary: What changed overnight is the pressure valve, not the pressure. DXY is 102.26, off yesterday's 100th-percentile print to the 95th, as EURUSD bounced +0.3% to 1.1194 off the 4th percentile, GBP +0.4%, AUD +0.7%, USDCAD -0.4% and the AUD/JPY risk cross +0.7%. Duration extended its bid: 10s -3bp to 5.21%, 30s -4bp to 5.56%, 5s -2bp to 5.00%, the 10-year real yield -3bp to 2.88%, TLT +1.4% on the week. Regime improves a tick to -6 from -7; rates composite stuck at -64, breadth at -17. That is relief in the two instruments everyone watches, nothing more.

Crude did not participate in the truce. WTI +1.6% to 95.62 and +8.3% on the week, Brent 106.55 (+75.1% YTD), DBC at the 98th percentile, oil/gold +7.8% on the week. Critically, RBOB is -3.1% on the day and -5.0% on the month: this is a crude-side bid, not a demand pull. And the market refuses to call it inflation — 5-year breakevens are 2.33%, -7bp on the month and rolling over, 10-year 2.33%. So the barrel lands on real yields and margins instead: DFII10 2.88%, +28bp in a month, z=1.03, the 95th percentile, and the 30-year mortgage at 7.40%, z=2.06 with acceleration 1.50, a fresh 52-week high. Oil up, breakevens down, real rates up is the worst combination for cyclicals.

The pain keeps migrating to the periphery rather than the index. USDMXN is 18.371, +0.6% today and +8.2% on the month at z=3.05 with acceleration 2.07 — still the most extreme reading in the book — while USDBRL is -1.8% on the month and Brazil compounds (EWZ +12.3% 1m, Bovespa +10.5%, z=1.77). Korea is the new epicentre of the silicon de-rating: KOSPI -11.7% on the week and -10.1% on the month (z=-1.56), EWY -10.6% on the week, MU -8.8%, TSM -7.7%, ASML -6.3%, SOXX -7.7% — while Taiwan is untouched, TWII +0.6% today and +6.0% on the month at the 95th percentile. The money stayed one layer up the stack: IGV +9.3% on the month, CIBR +13.8% with acceleration z=2.01, PLTR +24.8%, META +17.8%, MSFT at the 100th percentile. The S&P at 7805 and the 99th percentile, 7.5% above its 200-day, is hiding all of it: IWM/SPY at the 9th percentile (z=-1.61), RSP/SPY at the 12th, IYT/SPY at the 6th, XHB/SPY at the 1st.

Hedges remain mispriced against the stress that is actually visible. VIX 15.34 at the 11th percentile, VIX3M at the 5th, versus MOVE 101 (+23% on the month, z=1.19) and SKEW 155 at the 80th. Credit is still the bull's best card — credit composite 42, HYG/IEF at the 89th percentile, BKLN at the 91st — but HYG is rolling over at z=-1.01 and -1.5% on the month. The commodity complex sends the cleanest signal: copper +0.9% to 6.74 at the 96th percentile and copper/gold at the 100th with z=1.63 and acceleration 1.37, while gold is -4.4% on the month at the 15th percentile, silver -7.7%, GDX -10.2%. That says growth, not stress — and it flatly contradicts housing, transports, banks (GS -13.3% on the month at z=-1.91, BX -14.4%, KBE -7.0%) and the thematic graveyard: REMX -18.6% at the 0th percentile, NLR -12.2% at the 0th, uranium -14.1%, ITA -6.7% (z=-1.48), Turkey -15.7% (z=-1.91).

good.text: Duration rallied a third straight session and the dollar's vertical leg stalled against majors: 10s -3bp to 5.21%, 30s -4bp to 5.56%, real yield -3bp to 2.88%, TLT +1.4% on the week; EURUSD +0.3% off the 4th percentile, GBP +0.4%, AUD +0.7%, USDCAD -0.4%, DXY down from the 100th to the 95th percentile.

Copper keeps telling a growth story: +0.9% to 6.74 at the 96th percentile, copper/gold +1.3% on the day, +11.3% on the month, z=1.63 with acceleration 1.37 and a 52-week-high ratio. Risk crosses agree — AUD/JPY +0.7%.

Credit still refuses to confirm the equity-internals damage: HYG/IEF at the 89th percentile, BKLN at the 91st, credit composite up to 42 from 41, VIX 15.34. Nothing in spread-land is validating the bank tape yet.

Energy equity is the only sector with a clean uptrend and a 52-week high: XLE and XOP both at the 100th percentile, XOP +2.8%, XOM +1.1% at its high (rel strength +16.4% over 3m), CVX +1.3%; Canada TSX +0.9%, Brazil EWZ +12.3% on the month.

The AI trade rotated rather than broke: IGV +9.3% on the month (z=1.10), CIBR +13.8% with acceleration z=2.01, PLTR +24.8%, META +17.8%, MSFT +9.6% at the 100th percentile, and Europe caught a bid (DAX +0.6%, FTSE +2.2% on the week, both turning up).

bad.text: Crude re-accelerated into the dollar's pause and it is a supply bid, not demand: WTI +1.6% to 95.62 and +8.3% on the week, Brent 106.55, DBC at the 98th percentile — while RBOB is -3.1% on the day and -5.0% on the month. With 5y breakevens at 2.33% and falling, the barrel is a tax, and it lands on real yields: DFII10 2.88%, +28bp in a month, 95th percentile.

The peso is the accelerating accident: USDMXN 18.371, +0.6% today, +8.2% on the month, z=3.05 with acceleration 2.07, 5.3% above its 200-day. USDBRL +0.7% today too. EM FX stress is widening at the edges even as CEW holds.

Korea is being liquidated: KOSPI -11.7% on the week and -10.1% on the month (z=-1.56), EWY -10.6% on the week with acceleration z=-1.53, MU -8.8%, TSM -7.7%, ASML -6.3%, SOXX -7.7% — while Taiwan is +6.0% on the month at the 95th percentile. That geographic split is positioning unwinding, not a demand signal.

Housing and transport internals are at the bottom of the book while mortgage rates make new highs: 30-year mortgage 7.40%, +69bp on the month, z=2.06, acceleration 1.50, 100th percentile; ITB -12.1% over 3m at the 2nd percentile, XHB/SPY at the 1st, IYT/SPY at the 6th, IWM/SPY at the 9th (z=-1.61), RSP/SPY at the 12th.

Equity vol is priced for calm against a bond market that isn't: VIX at the 11th percentile, VIX3M at the 5th, versus MOVE 101 (+23% on the month, z=1.19) and SKEW 155. Meanwhile the curve flattens again (2s10s -6bp on the week, acceleration z=1.02) with the 3m bill at 4.26%, 97th percentile — no cuts being priced into the banks' funding costs. GS -13.3% on the month (z=-1.91), BX -14.4%, KBE -7.0%.

trades.name: Long XOP vs short IWM
trades.line: Long XOP vs short IWM: oil's third leg vs rate-squeezed smalls
trades.expr: Equal-dollar long XOP, short IWM. Cash ETFs or XLE/Russell-future variant for size; rebalance weekly to equal notional.
trades.thesis: Crude is the one asset still tightening financial conditions and it pays the producer directly, while small caps carry the cost of a 5.21% 10-year, a 7.40% mortgage and no front-end relief. The pair harvests both ends of the same shock.
trades.trigger: WTI +1.6% to 95.62 and +8.3% on the week, Brent 106.55; XOP +2.8% on the day at the 100th 52-week percentile with relative strength +16.6% over 3m and XLE also at the 100th. Against that, IWM/SPY sits at the 9th percentile, z=-1.61.
trades.stop: WTI closes below 88 (gives back the week and the 200-day premium) or the pair draws down 6% from entry.
trades.target: +10-12% on the pair; XOP relative strength extending another 8% vs the S&P.

trades.name: Short ITB into the mortgage spike
trades.line: Short ITB: 7.40% mortgage, z=2.06, and a dead-cat +0.8% bounce
trades.expr: Short ITB outright, or buy 3-month ~5% OTM ITB puts; pair against long SPY if you need beta-neutrality.
trades.thesis: The 30-year mortgage at a fresh 52-week high with acceleration z=1.50 is not yet in builder estimates. Even with 10s 3bp lower, primary mortgage rates are +69bp in a month — the transmission is in spreads, not the benchmark.
trades.trigger: MORTGAGE30US 7.40%, z=2.06, 100th percentile; ITB -12.1% over 3m, 11.8% below its 200-day, 2nd percentile — yet bounced +0.8% yesterday, giving a better entry. XHB/SPY at the 1st percentile, DHI -9.4% over 3m, HD -12.3%.
trades.stop: 30-year mortgage back under 7.00% or 10s under 4.95%; or ITB +8% from entry.
trades.target: ITB -12%; XHB/SPY to new 52-week relative lows.

trades.name: Long EWZ vs short EWW
trades.line: Long Brazil, short Mexico: BRL firm while the peso goes z=3.05
trades.expr: Long EWZ, short EWW, equal notional; or express in FX as short USDMXN-funded long BRL carry if you can run the spot book.
trades.thesis: LatAm has split. Brazil has falling USDBRL, a 10.5% monthly index gain and oil/commodity tailwinds; Mexico has a currency breaking at a 3-sigma pace with the equity market rolling over. Same region, opposite flows.
trades.trigger: USDMXN 18.371, +0.6% today, +8.2% on the month, z=3.05 with acceleration 2.07, the most extreme print in the digest; USDBRL -1.8% on the month. EWZ +12.3% on the month (z=1.37) at the 96th percentile, Bovespa +10.5% (z=1.77) vs EWW -2.8% and rolling over.
trades.stop: USDMXN back below 17.50, or the pair gives back 7%.
trades.target: +10% on the pair over the quarter.

trades.name: Buy index vol / downside convexity
trades.line: Buy SPX downside: VIX 11th pctile vs MOVE +23% on the month
trades.expr: December SPX put spread ~5%/12% out of the money, or a VIX Jan 20/30 call spread; budget 50-60bp of NAV.
trades.thesis: Equity vol is priced off the index, which is at the 99th percentile and 7.5% above its 200-day, while the market underneath it is already in a correction. Bond vol, FX vol (peso z=3.05) and the energy tape all argue the calm is an index artefact.
trades.trigger: VIX 15.34 at the 11th percentile, VIX3M at the 5th, term structure 0.85; against MOVE 101 (+23% on the month, z=1.19) and SKEW 155 at the 80th. HYG rolling over at z=-1.01 is the first crack in the one composite still supporting risk.
trades.stop: Breadth repairs — RSP/SPY and IWM/SPY turn up off the 12th/9th percentiles and HYG/IEF makes new highs; then cut and recycle. Hard cap at premium spent.

trades.name: Long IGV vs short SMH
trades.line: Long software vs semis: IGV/SMH +7.4% in a week, +21% in 3m
trades.expr: Long IGV, short SMH, equal notional; substitute CIBR for part of the long leg for the stronger momentum sleeve.
trades.thesis: The AI trade is de-rating hardware and re-rating the layer above it. The semi unwind is also geographically specific (Korea, memory) rather than demand-driven, which argues for relative, not outright, exposure.
trades.trigger: IGV +9.3% on the month at z=1.10 with acceleration 0.97, CIBR +13.8% with acceleration z=2.01, PLTR +24.8%; against SOXX -7.7% and SMH -7.0% on the week, MU -8.8%, TSM -7.7%. IGV/SMH +7.4% in a week and +21.0% over 3m.
trades.stop: IGV/SMH reverses 6% from entry or SMH reclaims its weekly loss with EWY/KOSPI stabilising.

trades.name: Long FCX vs short GDX
trades.line: Long copper equity, short gold miners: Cu/Au at a 52-wk high
trades.expr: Long FCX (or COPX for the basket), short GDX, equal notional.
trades.thesis: The metals complex has bifurcated completely: industrial demand is being bid while the monetary hedge is being liquidated. Owning the ratio in equities gets you operating leverage on both legs.
trades.trigger: Copper +0.9% to 6.74 at the 96th percentile; copper/gold +1.3% today, +11.3% on the month, z=1.63, acceleration 1.37, 100th percentile. Gold -4.4% on the month at the 15th percentile, silver -7.7%, GDX -10.2% with relative strength -12.0% and GDX/gold acceleration z=-1.57; GDXJ -2.0% on the day.
trades.stop: Gold reclaims its 200-day (currently 8.4% above spot) or copper/gold rolls back under its 200-day; pair stop 7%.

trades.name: Short KRE vs long SPY
trades.line: Short regional banks vs SPY: flatter curve, no cuts, bad marks
trades.expr: Short KRE, long SPY at equal notional (or 0.8x SPY for beta).
trades.thesis: Banks need a steeper curve and lower funding costs; they are getting the opposite, plus an earnings season already marking down the money-centre and alternatives complex. The index hides it; the pair monetises it.
trades.trigger: 2s10s -2bp on the day and -6bp on the week with acceleration z=1.02, while the 3m bill is +5bp on the week to 4.26% at the 97th percentile. KRE -6.0% on the month, KRE/SPY z=-1.06 at the 14th percentile; KBE -7.0%, IAI -6.5%, GS -13.3% (z=-1.91), BX -14.4%, JPM -6.5%; XLF relative strength -5.8% over 1m and rolling over.
trades.stop: 2s10s steepens 15bp from 0.42 with the 3m bill falling, or KRE/SPY reclaims its 200-day; pair stop 7%.
trades.target: KRE/SPY to new 52-week lows; +8-10% on the pair.
